title: Foot and Ankle Region Massage
summary: Purpose, anatomy, timing, and the standard for completing a proper Zura foot and ankle region massage.

sections.title: Purpose of Foot and Ankle Region Massage
paragraphs: Foot and ankle region massage helps release tension held in the feet and ankles, supports relaxation through the whole body, and prepares the client for a deeper wellness experience.
During foot and ankle region massage, watch carefully for tension, pain points, and stress areas. These areas tell you where the client needs more care and where you should spend extra time.

sections.title: Timing Standard
paragraphs: Follow the approved timing unless a pain area clearly needs more care.
list: Four hands: 5 minutes for the foot and ankle region.
Two hands: 8 minutes per foot and ankle region.
Spend extra time on pain areas — do not rush past tension or tender spots.

sections.title: You Are Not Done Until It Is Done
paragraphs: A foot and ankle region massage is complete only when the foot and ankle region shows clear improvement — not when the clock runs out.
list: The foot and ankle region feels soft.
The foot and ankle region looks reddish (healthy circulation response).
The foot and ankle region is flexible.
The foot and ankle region feels better for the client.
sections.closing: If the foot and ankle region is still tight, pale, stiff, or uncomfortable, continue working — especially on the pain and stress areas — until the standard is met.
